claims.title: Ancient settlement of the land
claims.summary: Hunter-gatherer peoples occupy what is now Brazil over many millennia, leaving rock art and ancient sites across the interior and the northeast.

sources.label: Indigenous Peoples (Indigenas)
sources.publisher: IBGE, Brazilian Institute of Geography and Statistics

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Brazil: From the thousand nations of the forest and coast to a Portuguese colony built on sugar, gold, and the largest slave economy of the Americas, and on to an empire, a republic, and a modern democracy.", terralore.co/country/BRA/chronicle#ev-10000bce-ancient-settlement-of-the-land, claim TL:BRA:event:10000bce:ancient-settlement-of-the-land, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Tupi-Guarani expansion
claims.summary: Tupi-Guarani-speaking peoples spread across the Atlantic coast and into the interior, developing the farming and village societies later encountered by Europeans.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Brazil: From the thousand nations of the forest and coast to a Portuguese colony built on sugar, gold, and the largest slave economy of the Americas, and on to an empire, a republic, and a modern democracy.", terralore.co/country/BRA/chronicle#ev-1-tupi-guarani-expansion, claim TL:BRA:event:1:tupi-guarani-expansion, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Complex Amazonian societies
claims.summary: Riverine peoples of Amazonia sustain substantial settled populations, managing forests and soils on a scale long underestimated by outsiders.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Brazil: From the thousand nations of the forest and coast to a Portuguese colony built on sugar, gold, and the largest slave economy of the Americas, and on to an empire, a republic, and a modern democracy.", terralore.co/country/BRA/chronicle#ev-1000-complex-amazonian-societies, claim TL:BRA:event:1000:complex-amazonian-societies, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Some thousand nations at contact
claims.summary: On the eve of European arrival, perhaps two to four million people in hundreds of distinct nations inhabit the territory of present-day Brazil.

sources.label: Indigenous Peoples (Indigenas)
sources.publisher: IBGE, Brazilian Institute of Geography and Statistics

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Brazil: From the thousand nations of the forest and coast to a Portuguese colony built on sugar, gold, and the largest slave economy of the Americas, and on to an empire, a republic, and a modern democracy.", terralore.co/country/BRA/chronicle#ev-1500-some-thousand-nations-at-contact, claim TL:BRA:event:1500:some-thousand-nations-at-contact, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Cabral claims Brazil for Portugal
claims.summary: Pedro Alvares Cabral makes landfall on the coast near present-day Porto Seguro and claims the land for the Portuguese crown.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Brazil: From the thousand nations of the forest and coast to a Portuguese colony built on sugar, gold, and the largest slave economy of the Americas, and on to an empire, a republic, and a modern democracy.", terralore.co/country/BRA/chronicle#ev-1500-cabral-claims-brazil-for-portugal, claim TL:BRA:event:1500:cabral-claims-brazil-for-portugal, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The sugar economy
claims.summary: Sugar plantations and mills worked by enslaved labour rise in Pernambuco and Bahia, making Brazil a leading producer and the colony's chief source of wealth.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Brazil: From the thousand nations of the forest and coast to a Portuguese colony built on sugar, gold, and the largest slave economy of the Americas, and on to an empire, a republic, and a modern democracy.", terralore.co/country/BRA/chronicle#ev-1530-the-sugar-economy, claim TL:BRA:event:1530:the-sugar-economy, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Transatlantic slave trade
claims.summary: Brazil becomes the largest single destination of the Atlantic slave trade, receiving roughly 4.8-5 million enslaved Africans over more than three centuries.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Brazil: From the thousand nations of the forest and coast to a Portuguese colony built on sugar, gold, and the largest slave economy of the Americas, and on to an empire, a republic, and a modern democracy.", terralore.co/country/BRA/chronicle#ev-1538-transatlantic-slave-trade, claim TL:BRA:event:1538:transatlantic-slave-trade, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Gold rush in Minas Gerais
claims.summary: The discovery of gold in the interior sets off a vast rush, founding towns such as Ouro Preto and shifting the colony's centre southward.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Brazil: From the thousand nations of the forest and coast to a Portuguese colony built on sugar, gold, and the largest slave economy of the Americas, and on to an empire, a republic, and a modern democracy.", terralore.co/country/BRA/chronicle#ev-1695-gold-rush-in-minas-gerais, claim TL:BRA:event:1695:gold-rush-in-minas-gerais, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The court moves to Rio
claims.summary: Fleeing Napoleon, the Portuguese royal court relocates to Rio de Janeiro, which becomes the seat of the empire and is opened to wider trade.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Brazil: From the thousand nations of the forest and coast to a Portuguese colony built on sugar, gold, and the largest slave economy of the Americas, and on to an empire, a republic, and a modern democracy.", terralore.co/country/BRA/chronicle#ev-1808-the-court-moves-to-rio, claim TL:BRA:event:1808:the-court-moves-to-rio, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Independence and the Empire
claims.summary: Dom Pedro proclaims independence at the Cry of Ipiranga and is acclaimed Emperor Pedro I, founding the Empire of Brazil.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Brazil: From the thousand nations of the forest and coast to a Portuguese colony built on sugar, gold, and the largest slave economy of the Americas, and on to an empire, a republic, and a modern democracy.", terralore.co/country/BRA/chronicle#ev-1822-independence-and-the-empire, claim TL:BRA:event:1822:independence-and-the-empire, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Reign of Pedro II begins
claims.summary: Pedro II assumes personal rule, beginning a long reign that brings political stability and the rise of the coffee economy.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Brazil: From the thousand nations of the forest and coast to a Portuguese colony built on sugar, gold, and the largest slave economy of the Americas, and on to an empire, a republic, and a modern democracy.", terralore.co/country/BRA/chronicle#ev-1840-reign-of-pedro-ii-begins, claim TL:BRA:event:1840:reign-of-pedro-ii-begins, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: War of the Triple Alliance
claims.summary: Brazil, Argentina, and Uruguay defeat Paraguay in the deadliest war in South American history, at enormous human and financial cost.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Brazil: From the thousand nations of the forest and coast to a Portuguese colony built on sugar, gold, and the largest slave economy of the Americas, and on to an empire, a republic, and a modern democracy.", terralore.co/country/BRA/chronicle#ev-1864-war-of-the-triple-alliance, claim TL:BRA:event:1864:war-of-the-triple-alliance, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Abolition of slavery
claims.summary: Princess Isabel signs the Lei Aurea, abolishing slavery without compensation; Brazil is the last country in the Americas to do so.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Brazil: From the thousand nations of the forest and coast to a Portuguese colony built on sugar, gold, and the largest slave economy of the Americas, and on to an empire, a republic, and a modern democracy.", terralore.co/country/BRA/chronicle#ev-1888-abolition-of-slavery, claim TL:BRA:event:1888:abolition-of-slavery, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Proclamation of the Republic
claims.summary: A military coup led by Marshal Deodoro da Fonseca deposes Pedro II and proclaims the Republic, ending the monarchy.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Brazil: From the thousand nations of the forest and coast to a Portuguese colony built on sugar, gold, and the largest slave economy of the Americas, and on to an empire, a republic, and a modern democracy.", terralore.co/country/BRA/chronicle#ev-1889-proclamation-of-the-republic, claim TL:BRA:event:1889:proclamation-of-the-republic, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: First republican constitution
claims.summary: The Constitution of 1891 establishes a federal republic with strong states, modelled in part on the United States.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Brazil: From the thousand nations of the forest and coast to a Portuguese colony built on sugar, gold, and the largest slave economy of the Americas, and on to an empire, a republic, and a modern democracy.", terralore.co/country/BRA/chronicle#ev-1891-first-republican-constitution, claim TL:BRA:event:1891:first-republican-constitution, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: War of Canudos
claims.summary: The army crushes a large millenarian community in the Bahian backlands, exposing the gulf between the republican coast and the impoverished interior.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Brazil: From the thousand nations of the forest and coast to a Portuguese colony built on sugar, gold, and the largest slave economy of the Americas, and on to an empire, a republic, and a modern democracy.", terralore.co/country/BRA/chronicle#ev-1896-war-of-canudos, claim TL:BRA:event:1896:war-of-canudos, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Mass immigration
claims.summary: Millions of immigrants, especially Italians, Portuguese, Spaniards, and Japanese, arrive to work coffee and settle the south, reshaping Brazilian society.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Brazil: From the thousand nations of the forest and coast to a Portuguese colony built on sugar, gold, and the largest slave economy of the Americas, and on to an empire, a republic, and a modern democracy.", terralore.co/country/BRA/chronicle#ev-1888-mass-immigration, claim TL:BRA:event:1888:mass-immigration, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Revolution of 1930
claims.summary: A disputed election amid the Depression brings down the Old Republic, and Getulio Vargas takes power, beginning a new era.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Brazil: From the thousand nations of the forest and coast to a Portuguese colony built on sugar, gold, and the largest slave economy of the Americas, and on to an empire, a republic, and a modern democracy.", terralore.co/country/BRA/chronicle#ev-1930-revolution-of-1930, claim TL:BRA:event:1930:revolution-of-1930, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The Estado Novo
claims.summary: Vargas imposes a centralised dictatorship, ruling by decree, banning parties, and censoring the press until his ouster in 1945.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Brazil: From the thousand nations of the forest and coast to a Portuguese colony built on sugar, gold, and the largest slave economy of the Americas, and on to an empire, a republic, and a modern democracy.", terralore.co/country/BRA/chronicle#ev-1937-the-estado-novo, claim TL:BRA:event:1937:the-estado-novo, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Inauguration of Brasilia
claims.summary: The purpose-built modernist capital, designed by Lucio Costa and Oscar Niemeyer, is inaugurated in the interior, shifting Brazil's centre of gravity inland.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Brazil: From the thousand nations of the forest and coast to a Portuguese colony built on sugar, gold, and the largest slave economy of the Americas, and on to an empire, a republic, and a modern democracy.", terralore.co/country/BRA/chronicle#ev-1960-inauguration-of-brasilia, claim TL:BRA:event:1960:inauguration-of-brasilia, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Military coup
claims.summary: The armed forces overthrow President Joao Goulart and seize power, beginning twenty-one years of military dictatorship.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Brazil: From the thousand nations of the forest and coast to a Portuguese colony built on sugar, gold, and the largest slave economy of the Americas, and on to an empire, a republic, and a modern democracy.", terralore.co/country/BRA/chronicle#ev-1964-military-coup, claim TL:BRA:event:1964:military-coup, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Institutional Act Number Five
claims.summary: AI-5 suspends habeas corpus and civil liberties, opening the regime's most repressive phase of censorship, torture, and disappearances.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Brazil: From the thousand nations of the forest and coast to a Portuguese colony built on sugar, gold, and the largest slave economy of the Americas, and on to an empire, a republic, and a modern democracy.", terralore.co/country/BRA/chronicle#ev-1968-institutional-act-number-five, claim TL:BRA:event:1968:institutional-act-number-five, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Return to civilian rule
claims.summary: After a gradual political opening, the military hands power back to civilians, ending the dictatorship.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Brazil: From the thousand nations of the forest and coast to a Portuguese colony built on sugar, gold, and the largest slave economy of the Americas, and on to an empire, a republic, and a modern democracy.", terralore.co/country/BRA/chronicle#ev-1985-return-to-civilian-rule, claim TL:BRA:event:1985:return-to-civilian-rule, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The Citizen Constitution
claims.summary: A new constitution restores full democracy and enshrines an expansive charter of civil, political, and social rights.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Brazil: From the thousand nations of the forest and coast to a Portuguese colony built on sugar, gold, and the largest slave economy of the Americas, and on to an empire, a republic, and a modern democracy.", terralore.co/country/BRA/chronicle#ev-1988-the-citizen-constitution, claim TL:BRA:event:1988:the-citizen-constitution, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Plano Real ends hyperinflation
claims.summary: A new currency and stabilisation plan tame runaway inflation, reshaping the economy and politics of the 1990s.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Brazil: From the thousand nations of the forest and coast to a Portuguese colony built on sugar, gold, and the largest slave economy of the Americas, and on to an empire, a republic, and a modern democracy.", terralore.co/country/BRA/chronicle#ev-1994-plano-real-ends-hyperinflation, claim TL:BRA:event:1994:plano-real-ends-hyperinflation, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Lula and social inclusion
claims.summary: Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva's governments expand social programmes during a commodities boom, lifting millions out of poverty.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Brazil: From the thousand nations of the forest and coast to a Portuguese colony built on sugar, gold, and the largest slave economy of the Americas, and on to an empire, a republic, and a modern democracy.", terralore.co/country/BRA/chronicle#ev-2003-lula-and-social-inclusion, claim TL:BRA:event:2003:lula-and-social-inclusion, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Impeachment amid Lava Jato
claims.summary: President Dilma Rousseff is impeached as the sweeping Car Wash corruption investigation reshapes Brazilian politics.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Brazil: From the thousand nations of the forest and coast to a Portuguese colony built on sugar, gold, and the largest slave economy of the Americas, and on to an empire, a republic, and a modern democracy.", terralore.co/country/BRA/chronicle#ev-2016-impeachment-amid-lava-jato, claim TL:BRA:event:2016:impeachment-amid-lava-jato, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Brasilia attacked, democracy holds
claims.summary: Supporters of the defeated president storm the Congress, presidential palace, and Supreme Court; the institutions withstand the assault.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Brazil: From the thousand nations of the forest and coast to a Portuguese colony built on sugar, gold, and the largest slave economy of the Americas, and on to an empire, a republic, and a modern democracy.", terralore.co/country/BRA/chronicle#ev-2023-brasilia-attacked-democracy-holds, claim TL:BRA:event:2023:brasilia-attacked-democracy-holds, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.
